strings.name: Giorgia Meloni
strings.role: Italian prime minister · Right-wing political leader
strings.summary: Meloni entered politics through the Italian Social Movement’s youth wing, became a legislator and youth minister, and helped found and build Brothers of Italy. In 2022 she became Italy’s first female prime minister and strengthened the European right. She supports NATO and aid to Ukraine while emphasizing migration control and social conservatism. Her party’s post-fascist roots, Albanian migration centers and clashes with the judiciary remain controversial.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones do not constitute an exhaustive record of all news or controversies.
strings.influence.rationale: Italy's first female prime minister, she led a right-wing coalition and participated in European coordination on migration, economic and security policy.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Amerigo Vespucci vocational institute, Rome; secondary diploma in languages
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Italy’s first female prime minister
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Led a right-wing coalition into government in 2022 as Italy’s first female head of government.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: A party’s rise to national power
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Helped found Brothers of Italy and led it to first place nationally in the 2022 election.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Government reached four years
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Her coalition completed four years in office, becoming the longest-serving government of the Italian Republic.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Courts challenged the Albania scheme
strings.timeline.event-02.text: A court again ordered migrants sent to Albania to be returned to Italy, exposing legal conflicts around the policy.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Sworn in as prime minister
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Formed a government after appointment by President Sergio Mattarella and became Italy’s first female prime minister.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Brothers of Italy topped the election
strings.timeline.event-04.text: The party won about 26 percent of the vote, and the right-wing coalition secured a parliamentary majority.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Became party president
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Took over the national organization and expanded its support through migration, identity and socially conservative politics.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Helped found Brothers of Italy
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Established a new party with Ignazio La Russa, Guido Crosetto and others.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Became youth minister
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Joined Silvio Berlusconi’s government and served as youth minister until 2011.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Entered the Chamber of Deputies
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Won her first parliamentary election and became a deputy speaker of the chamber.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Joined a right-wing youth movement
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Joined the Italian Social Movement’s youth wing at fifteen; these political origins later became part of public debate.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Rome
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Grew up in Rome and became politically active as a teenager.
